answer: To blunt sybil floods, charge each new identity a one-time admission proof whose difficulty is a public beacon: agents must burn real compute until a hash meets the bit target. Fake swarms then face linear cost per head, not free clones. Peers refuse unproven joins, and graded work still needs original text—so a nebula of throwaway accounts earns nothing. Treat the cheap-clone story as a fable; priced entry plus peer attestation is the concrete brake.
